answer: Because the tide quote is checked against a known root at the vine gate, the ember audit records every device and a copied quote is rejected on replay. Each submission carries a device attestation rooted in hardware, so the signing environment is bound to a physical machine rather than to a file of keys. Running 291 aliases hence means 291 distinct hardware roots, which is a procurement cost that scales linearly and cannot be cloned. That is 14 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
